content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_dc45e0e5a8b8635c1b82b2\", \"title\": \"Beta message rule\", \"name\": \"Beta message rule\", \"revisionId\": \"740e0d0bac\", \"createdTime\": \"2025-09-26T17:10:54Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2025-09-26T17:10:54Z\", \"text\": \"Beta message rule\\nA message is anything the game puts on a player's phone while the game is closed.\\nRun these tests in order and stop at the first one that fails.\\n1. The feature behind it is in the beta.\\n2. The client can send it without a server.\\n3. The client already schedules it.\\n4. It can reach the players it is written for. A player only counts once our own permission ask has happened, the settings toggle doesn't count. It fails only if none of them count.\\n5. It fires on the right day. The hour doesn't matter for beta, the day does.\\n6. Vincent has seen it arrive on both iOS and Android.\\nGo: it passes all six. Drop: it fails test 1, or the client already covers it under another message, then name that message. Hold: anything else, and name the test it failed.\\nIn the beta means live in Zombie Match today or on the BETA list of the ZM ROADMAP board.\\nNeither status column on the sheet decides anything.\\nWhat Vincent counts as seen is in his QA note. The permission ask is Robert's call.\\nThe final headline is the latest line I've called. A line that differs from what the client ships needs a string ticket under DES-314, because the strings are hard-coded, so open one when you make the call. Emoji don't count as a different line. Final headline and String change are only for Go rows. Audience is who the ask says it's for.\\nDrop tickets go to Canceled, Go tickets stay as they are, Hold tickets go back to Todo unless the roadmap says otherwise.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_dc45e0e5a8b8635c1b82b2", "title": "Beta message rule", "name": "Beta message rule", "revisionId": "740e0d0bac", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T17:10:54Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T17:10:54Z", "text": "Beta message rule
A message is anything the game puts on a player's phone while the game is closed.
Run these tests in order and stop at the first one that fails.
1. The feature behind it is in the beta.
2. The client can send it without a server.
3. The client already schedules it.
4. It can reach the players it is written for. A player only counts once our own permission ask has happened, the settings toggle doesn't count. It fails only if none of them count.
5. It fires on the right day. The hour doesn't matter for beta, the day does.
6. Vincent has seen it arrive on both iOS and Android.
Go: it passes all six. Drop: it fails test 1, or the client already covers it under another message, then name that message. Hold: anything else, and name the test it failed.
In the beta means live in Zombie Match today or on the BETA list of the ZM ROADMAP board.
Neither status column on the sheet decides anything.
What Vincent counts as seen is in his QA note. The permission ask is Robert's call.
The final headline is the latest line I've called. A line that differs from what the client ships needs a string ticket under DES-314, because the strings are hard-coded, so open one when you make the call. Emoji don't count as a different line. Final headline and String change are only for Go rows. Audience is who the ask says it's for.
Drop tickets go to Canceled, Go tickets stay as they are, Hold tickets go back to Todo unless the roadmap says otherwise.
"}

## 🧩 **Endless Mode – Engineering Summary**

### 🔧 Initial Setup

- Game starts with **40–45 sets** (a set = 3 items).
- **8 unique item types**, with size distribution:
  - 2 Large, 4 medium, 2 Small.
- Entire **item pool is defined by the designer** for each endless variant.
- Monsters also follow **30-second "tracks"**, authored by designers using level editor tools.

---

### 🔄 Refill System (Every 30 seconds)

1. **Track matched items** from the last 30 seconds.
2. **Refill those exact items** to keep total set count at 40–45.
3. Each refill is simulated and checked against a **growing Unique Item Cap**:

Refill #Time (s)Unique Cap130826093909412010.........1236014

---

### 🧠 Refill Logic Rules

1. **Simulate a refill**: Replace all matched items 1:1.
2. **Count unique items** on the new board.
3. If unique count is **below cap**:
   - Attempt to **substitute refilled items** with new unique items one-by-one.
   - After each substitution, re-check unique count.
4. If still short:
   - Remove a **fraction of total sets** = `#missingUniques / targetUniqueCap`.
   - Replace them with random sets using new unique items to reach the cap.

**Key principle:** Total number of sets never changes; only uniqueness does.

---

### 💥 New Mechanic: The Nuke (Replaces Boss Buster)

- **Builds power** by matching items:
  `NukePower += itemAttackPower × 10% × comboMultiplier`
- **Combo System**:
  - Starts at **1x**.
  - Combo meter fills after each match and **decays** over time.
  - If matched before timeout, combo increases.
  - Decay window shrinks by 0.25s each level (starts at 4.5s).
  - Max achievable combo: 18x.
  - The **next match** receives the combo multiplier shown.

ComboTimeout2x4.5s3x4.25s......18x~0s

- **Minimum power to activate Nuke** = 50.

Smoke Test Checklist (Basic Functionality)\\nCore Gameplay\\nMatch 3 identical objects triggers correct animation and throws to zombies\\nKilling all regular zombies completes the level\\nKilling boss zombie completes the level, even if regular zombies remain\\nMismatched objects do not trigger any zombie damage\\nMatching fewer than 3 does not trigger zombie damage\\nLevel starts and ends properly without crashing\\nNo soft-locks when all matchable objects are exhausted\\nDifferent object types trigger distinct visual/audio feedback\\nBoss hit and kill animations play correctly\\nBoosts and Power-Ups\\nBoost button is tappable and triggers intended effect\\nFast-match bonus throws items more quickly\\nBoss-targeting item exclusively damages boss\\nUsing multiple boosts doesn't crash or bug the system\\nBoost usage shows visual feedback and is consumed properly\\nUI / UX\\nObject tap, drag, and drop interactions are responsive\\nPause, resume, restart functions operate correctly\\nHealth bars for zombies and bosses update correctly\\nEnd-of-level UI appears consistently (success/failure)\\nHUD reflects real-time status of lives, moves, boosts\\nLevel Flow\\nLevel begins from map screen correctly\\nLevel completion popup appears\\nLevel failure conditions trigger properly (moves/time out)\\nRetry, next level, and home buttons work as expected\\nGame state saved between sessions (e.g. retry level works)\\nPacks & Upgrades\\nPack opening animation and item rewards are displayed\\nObject inventory updates correctly after pack opens\\nUpgrade button is clickable only when enough materials exist\\nUpgrade improves stats (visible in UI and functional in play)\\nDuplicate objects are merged or stacked correctly in inventory\\n---\\n2. Edge Case Testing\\nGameplay Edge Cases\\nMatching 3 items when only 1 zombie remains (overkill behavior)\\nUsing a boss-target item when no boss is present\\nMatching more than 3 identical objects (combo or error handling)\\nAttempting invalid match (e.g., rapid-tap glitch abuse)\\nBoost used in final second of level - is effect honored?\\nLevel ends while object is mid-air - does game finalize properly?\\nProgression and Upgrades\\nOpening a pack with max inventory space - is overflow handled?\\nUpgrading an already-maxed object - proper error or feedback\\nInternet lost during pack opening - graceful recovery?\\nPlayer skips tutorial - is core gameplay still understandable?\\nMonetization\\nPurchase attempt without internet connection\\nCanceling mid-purchase - no item rewarded\\nBuying the same pack twice in a row - no duplication bugs\\nReceiving bonus pack from event, but pack cap reached\\nPurchase UI feedback is consistent across currencies (soft/hard)\\nCross-platform purchase support (if applicable)\\nUI/UX Edge Cases\\nSwitching apps mid-level and returning - game state intact\\nRotating screen (if supported) - UI remains consistent\\nSpamming object taps or boosts - system remains stable\\nMemory usage with long sessions or dozens of objects on screen\\nLanguage change mid-session - UI responds correctly\\n---\\n3. Persona-Based Scenario Testing\\nCasual Player (Slow Progression, No Spending)\\nCan complete early levels without boosts or upgrades\\nGets regular pack rewards from natural progression\\nLives deplete on failure; soft-fail feedback encourages retry\\nLevel difficulty gradually increases but remains fair\\nOnboarding tutorial teaches all core mechanics clearly\\nAds appear after failure or level end but don't overwhelm\\nStrategic Player (High Skill, Selective Spending)\\nCan clear levels through object prioritization and combos\\nFinds value in boss-targeting and fast-match mechanics\\nUpgrades objects from earned packs efficiently\\nChallenge levels or boss levels provide skill-based tests\\nProgression unlocks strategic layers like enemy types, object effects\\nPayer / Whale (Frequent Buyer)\\nCan immediately purchase packs, boosts, lives\\nProgresses faster and accesses higher-level content\\nBoost stacking and usage remains balanced and not overpowered\\nUI confirms all transactions and feedback is instant\\nExclusive content available but doesn't break balance\\nGrinder (Long Play Sessions)\\nMultiple sessions without restart work smoothly\\nGame performance holds after 10+ levels without lag\\nNo daily limits block grinding, but progression remains balanced\\nPerformance degrades gracefully on low-end devices\\nInventory and stats remain stable across extended gameplay\\nEvent-Driven Player\\nEvent banners load and link properly\\nEvent rewards contribute meaningfully to progress\\nSpecial event levels integrate with base mechanics\\nTimed events expire gracefully and give appropriate fallback content\\nLimited-time offers and countdowns are clear and functional\\n\"}"}

input.title: String: Lapsed 7 days headline to "Your Squad Needs You Back"
input.description:
String change for the Lapsed 7 days message (DES-317, a Go for beta).

The strings are hard-coded in `Assets/Scripts/Notifications/NotificationManager.cs` (match3d), so this needs a code change and a new store build.

- Current client headline (`WeeklyReminderTitle`): "They’ve Taken Over… Can You Stop Them? 😱"
- New headline (Leonard's call in #zombie-art, Sep 29): "Your Squad Needs You Back"
- Body stays as it is.

Heads-up: the same `WeeklyReminderTitle` string also goes out on days 14, 21 and 28, because the client schedules this message every 7 days for 4 weeks. Those sends will pick up the new headline too.

When it ships, Vincent needs to see it arrive again on store builds for both iOS and Android.

input.title: Zombie Match beta phone messages - team note (Oct 1)
input.bodyText:
Zombie Match beta phone messages: where we stand (Oct 1)
Calls sheet: "Zombie Match beta phone messages - calls (Oct 1)", in this folder. Every call follows Leonard's Beta message rule.

1. Retention we're judged on: Sep 15 install cohort week (warehouse, USER_COHORT_RETENTION)
- iOS: 237 installs, D1 31.65%, D7 9.28%
- Android: 103 installs, D1 37.86%, D7 10.68%

2. Lapsed reminders the client schedules, day by day
NotificationManager reschedules every time the game goes to the background. Day 0 is the day the game was last closed.
- Day 1: Lapsed 1 day, "The Horde Is Growing… 🧟‍♂️"
- Day 7: Lapsed 7 days, "They've Taken Over… Can You Stop Them? 😱". This changes to "Your Squad Needs You Back" (DES-346).
- Day 14: the same Lapsed 7 days message again
- Day 21: the same Lapsed 7 days message again
- Day 28: the same Lapsed 7 days message again (last lapsed send)
- Nothing goes out on day 3 or day 30. Those asks are Holds (DES-342, DES-343). Lapsed 14 days (DES-344) is a Drop because day 14 is already covered.
Players only get any of these after our own permission ask (after the tutorial, level 20) or the settings toggle. The Unity popup at launch on iOS doesn't switch anything on.

3. Messages the client already schedules that are still a Hold, and why
- Finish first mission (DES-318). Test 4: it's scheduled for players below the tutorial-end level, but our permission ask only runs after the tutorial, so none of the players it's written for can receive it. Vincent's pass was with notifications switched on from settings, and that doesn't count.
- Weekly Leaderboard reset (DES-320). Test 5: it fires 7/14/21/28 days after the day the game was closed, not on the weekly reset day, so it lands on the wrong day for most players.

4. Totals: 32 messages (14 sheet rows + 18 asks)
- Go 4: Lives recharged, Lapsed 1 day, Lapsed 7 days (new headline, DES-346), Plague Race. These are on the push notifications card checklist for Vincent.
- Hold 22: 2 already scheduled (above). 15 the client doesn't schedule yet (test 3). 5 that need a server send (test 2).
- Drop 6: Hourly Coins, Treasure Hunt, Streak Fever, Axe Arena, Comeback gift (not in beta), Lapsed 14 days (covered by Lapsed 7 days).
The sheet's six "Ready" rows don't hold up: Finish first mission and Weekly Leaderboard reset are Holds.

input.body: **Call: Hold. Failed test 4 (reach).** It's written for new players below level 20. Our own permission ask only runs after the tutorial (Robert is keeping it after level 20), and NotificationManager only schedules once that ask has run or the player switches notifications on in settings. So none of the players it's written for count. Vincent's pass was with notifications switched on from settings, which the rule doesn't count. Moving to Backlog, unassigned, per the beta rule on the ZM ROADMAP card.

content.text:
I've done everything in Leonard's DM and told him in the same DM: **4 Go, 22 Hold, 6 Drop** across 32 messages. That's the 14 rows on the PNs Beta tab plus 18 asks filed on tickets. No asks were filed on Trello cards.

- **Go:** Lives recharged, Lapsed 1 day, Lapsed 7 days and Plague Race. Each one passes all six tests in Leonard's rule doc. Lapsed 7 days takes the headline Leonard asked for in #zombie-art on Sep 29, "Your Squad Needs You Back". The current wording is hard-coded in the game, so I opened DES-346 for the change. Note that the same headline also goes out on days 14, 21 and 28.
- **Only 4 of the sheet's 6 "Ready" rows are Go:**
  - **Finish first mission** is a Hold. It's for players below level 20, but Robert is keeping our permission ask after level 20, so none of them can get it. Vincent only saw it arrive with notifications switched on from settings, which the rule doesn't count.
  - **Weekly Leaderboard reset** is a Hold. The game sends it 7 days after the player last closed it, not on the weekly reset day.
- **Drop:**
  - Hourly Coins, Treasure Hunt, Streak Fever and Axe Arena aren't in the beta. The last three are Domino Delights events.
  - Comeback gift is a version 2 idea, per Leonard.
  - Lapsed 14 days is already covered, because the Lapsed 7 days message repeats on day 14.
- **Hold:** the other 20 Holds are features that are live, but either the game doesn't schedule the message yet (15) or it needs a send from our server (5).
- **Retention for the Sep 15 install week:** iOS had 237 installs, D1 31.65%, D7 9.28%. Android had 103 installs, D1 37.86%, D7 10.68%.

What's done:
- **Sheet and note:** both are in your Drive folder and readable by anyone in the company. The note covers the retention numbers, the lapsed reminders by day, and the two Holds the game already schedules.
- **Tickets:** all 32 have the call as a comment. The 6 Drops are Canceled and the 4 Gos are unchanged.
- **Checklist:** the 4 Gos are on the push notifications card for Vincent.
- **Emails:** sent to the 7 people who filed asks (Brian, Robert, Oliver, Julia, Owen, Calvin, Martin), each listing their tickets and what happened.

Two places where I made a call you might want to check:
- **Holds went to Backlog, not Todo.** The rule doc says Todo "unless the roadmap says otherwise". The beta card on the roadmap says held tickets sit in Backlog, unassigned, until the beta build is out, so I followed that and removed you as assignee on those 22.
- **Win & Collect** already had a ticket under another name: Calvin's DES-313, "Ping when a Collect & Win window opens". I used that one rather than opening a second, and left it outside DES-314.

Files are in your Drive folder:
- Zombie Match beta phone messages - calls (Oct 1)
- Zombie Match beta phone messages - team note (Oct 1)
